## [How Jill finds candidates](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/search-and-candidate-discovery\#how-jill-finds-candidates)

Jill searches Jack’s network: a six-figure pool of professionals who each have an ongoing relationship with Jack. Jack knows their skills, experience, career goals, and what they’re looking for in their next role.

When you create a role, Jill builds a [hiring brief](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/hiring-brief) from your description and uses it to search across this network. She’s not matching keywords on a résumé. She looks at hard skills, but also soft factors like work environment fit and career trajectory. The result is candidates who are more likely to succeed on your team.

Jill runs searches continuously. As new people join Jack’s network or update their preferences, she’ll surface them if they match your brief.

## [Search](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/search-and-candidate-discovery\#search)

Open a role’s **Candidates** tab to browse the candidates Jill has found in Jack’s network. During your [setup conversation](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/getting-started#the-setup-conversation), you and Jill define evaluation criteria together — the specific things that matter for this role (e.g. “has built a team from scratch,” “strong systems design,” “startup pace”). Jill evaluates candidates against those criteria.

The overall fit label on a candidate (such as **Excellent** or **Good**) reflects Jill’s recommendation for this role. It isn’t a percentage match or an average of the individual criteria scores. Open a candidate to review the criteria, experience, and education before deciding whether to save them or pass.

Saved candidates move to the **Saved** stage in that role’s [Pipeline](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/pipeline-management), where you can return to them and request introductions.

Jill continues searching and sends you candidate updates by email or Slack on the days you choose.

## [Candidate signals](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/search-and-candidate-discovery\#candidate-signals)

Search result cards may show a **Recently started** badge when a candidate’s current-role start date suggests a recent move. Some profiles have only a year, so check their experience for the exact timing. Indicators such as **Saved** and **Reached out** reflect the hiring workflow, not the candidate’s availability.

A candidate’s own job-search status stays private between them and Jack; it isn’t shown to hiring teams in Jill.

## [Giving Jill feedback](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/search-and-candidate-discovery\#giving-jill-feedback)

The more context you give Jill, the better her searches become. You can give feedback in several ways.

- **Chat with Jill**: Tell her what’s working and what isn’t. Tell her “I need people with more backend experience”, and she’ll adjust the next search immediately.
- **Save or pass on candidates**: Your choices help Jill learn what you’re looking for. You can also add a note when you pass, explaining why someone wasn’t a fit. Learn more about candidate notes in [Pipeline Management](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/pipeline-management#candidate-notes).
- **Share reference profiles**: If you know someone who embodies what you’re looking for, share their LinkedIn profile. Jill uses reference profiles to understand your ideal candidate more concretely.

Think of it as a conversation, not a one-shot search. The brief is a starting point: your feedback makes it sharper over time.

## [Excluding candidates already in your ATS](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/search-and-candidate-discovery\#excluding-candidates-already-in-your-ats)

If you’ve connected your ATS, you can hide people who are already in it, so you don’t ask for an introduction to someone your team is already talking to. This is available for Ashby in the new Jill workspace. For other ATSs, contact us to confirm it’s available for your account. The earlier Jill app can show people in your ATS but doesn’t have the option to hide them.

To do this, Jill needs to be able to see who is in your ATS, including people who didn’t come from Jack & Jill. That access comes from an optional addendum to our Data Processing Agreement (DPA) called **2\. Additional ATS Processing And Sharing Activities**. Your company agrees to it once, and an admin does it while connecting your ATS. Without it, Jill only knows about candidates she sent to your ATS herself, so the filter isn’t offered.

**To turn it on**

1. When you connect your ATS, agree to the core Data Processing Agreement, then also agree to **2\. Additional ATS Processing And Sharing Activities (optional)**. Agreeing there lets Jill read people already in your ATS.
2. Link the role to its job in your ATS, as described in your ATS integration guide. Jill then reads the job’s applications in the background. The filter appears once that finishes, which takes a few minutes for most roles and up to a few hours for roles with thousands of applications. Check back later.

Greenhouse and Lever connect through the provider’s own sign-in screen, which doesn’t offer this step. The same goes for any ATS connected before this option existed, or where it was skipped. For these, agree to the terms under **Settings → Legal**, which records your agreement but doesn’t switch the reading on. Then contact us and we’ll enable it.

Teamtailor needs one more thing: Jill can only read your existing Teamtailor candidates with an Admin API key with Read. A Public key doesn’t allow it, and the filter won’t appear however long you wait. See [Importing candidates that already exist](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/teamtailor-ats-integration#importing-candidates-that-already-exist).

**To exclude people already in your ATS**

1. Open the role’s **Candidates** tab.
2. Choose **Filter**, then **In your ATS**, and select **No**.

Select **Yes** to see only the people already in your ATS, or **Any** to see everyone again. People who are in your ATS show an **In your ATS** label with their current stage, so you can spot them even when the filter is off.

A few things to know:

- The filter is per role. “In your ATS” means the person has an application on the ATS job linked to this role, so someone who is only in your ATS for a different job isn’t hidden.
- Jill matches people by email address and, where your ATS provides it, their LinkedIn profile. If someone’s email in your ATS differs from the one they use with Jack, and your ATS doesn’t give us their LinkedIn profile, they won’t be flagged. Jill would rather miss someone than flag the wrong person.
- It changes what you see, not what Jill searches for. Nobody is removed from the role or from your ATS.
- If **In your ATS** isn’t under **Filter**, the role may not be linked yet, its applications may still be loading, or reading existing candidates may not be switched on for your company. Ask an admin to check the last of these.

You can also ask Jill, for example “How do I hide people who are already in our ATS?” She’ll point you to the filter and check the role’s ATS link. She can’t see whether reading existing candidates is switched on, so she’ll ask an admin to confirm it if the filter is missing.

## [Public Profiles](https://www.jackandjill.ai/docs/search-and-candidate-discovery\#public-profiles)

In addition to Jack’s network, you can search Public Profiles, a vast pool of publicly available profiles from LinkedIn and other platforms. Jill scores these candidates against your brief and explains her reasoning, just like she does with Jack’s network. The difference is that there’s no warm introduction. You reach out directly through LinkedIn or your preferred channel. We take no credit or fee from Public Profile hires: they’re there to support hiring teams in areas where our network is sparser.
